positions.subject: contest:2026-ca-general/prop-40
positions.summary: Her campaign spokesperson told SFGATE in August 2026 that she supports Proposition 40; The Intercept reported in May 2026 that she favored the statewide billionaire tax.

citations.quote: Krager said that despite her absence, Chan is in support of it.

Both of Wiener’s opponents in the three-way June 2 primary — progressive member of San Francisco’s board of supervisors Connie Chan and Justice Democrats co-founder Saikat Chakrabarti — are in favor of the taxes.

positions.subject: q:ai/data-center-moratorium
positions.summary: Supports a national data center moratorium until stronger protections exist for communities, utilities, and the environment.

positions.subject: q:healthcare/single-payer
positions.summary: Supports Medicare for All; also seeks restored Medicaid funding and extended ACA subsidies.

positions.subject: q:housing/transit-oriented-upzoning
positions.summary: In July 2025 she introduced a Board of Supervisors resolution opposing SB 79, saying it undercut San Francisco's community process for its Housing Element and would circumvent the city's zoning rules; the board rejected the resolution 7-4 on July 22, 2025.

citations.quote: The measure “undercuts the years-long community process to develop a citywide Housing Element," reads the text of a resolution introduced by Supervisor Connie Chan to signal opposition to the measure.
Chan’s resolution failed to pass after the Board of Supervisors voted against it 7-4 at their July 22 meeting.
Wiener’s proposal would circumvent the city’s zoning rules and lead to “land speculation, displacement and gentrification,” according to Chan.
The resolution, by Sups. Connie Chan, Chyanne Chen, and Jackie Fielder, urges the Legislature to defeat the bill

positions.subject: q:taxes/federal-wealth-tax
